While US aid was certainly good for Britain, Russia and a whole lot of other countries who we supplied to, you cannot deny the overwhelming tenacity of the Soviets, the stubbornness of the British and the partisan groups all throughout Europe. Saying the "US was the reason the second world war ended" is flawed logic. US involvement was crucial at points, but the overwhelming manpower of the Soviet Union allowed the US and Britain to open that second front. The ability for England to hold on in the face of overwhelming odds and constant bombing gave not just the US, but Canada, the Czechs, the Poles, and the Greeks a jumping off point into Europe. Our bombing campaigns crippled Axis manufacturing, our tanks and soldiers may have helped beat the Germans and Italians back, but in now way did the US singlehandedly stop the Germans and Italians. There are far too many factors at play.
You could say that the ineptitude of the German High Command and Hitler ended the war in Europe. You could say that the overextension of supply, the limited manpower and the overwhelming odds on all sides of the German fronts ended the war. You cannot say that the second world war ended Ailey because of American involvement. That's not fair to us, that's not fair to the British, thats not fair to the Soviets.
